transcript.text: Hi Harsh, thanks for joining. Today I'd like to go through your resume in some detail and hear the stories behind it. We have about 15 minutes, with time for your questions at the end. Tell me about a sales skill you picked up recently in your MBA.
transcript.why: This was a warm-up question to help you settle in. It isn't part of the feedback.

transcript.text: Achha toh basically, ekdum recent wala sales skill jo maine pick kiya hai na IIML mein, woh consultative selling hai, pehle jab family business mein tha tab zyada transactional approach hota tha matlab product dikhao, rate batao, deal close karo, lekin yahan pe kya hota hai ki matlab humne ek course mein case studies ki thi, jismein focus tha ki pehle samjho client ko kya pain point hai, fir apna solution customise karke pitch karna, matlab unko feel ho ki unke liye hi bana hai, toh ek example bolu toh markstrat simulation mein humne ek segment select kiya tha jahan pe competitors zyada aggressive the, toh I went and actually tried to talk to team mates as if they're customers, poocha unko kya chahiye, kis price pe lenge, aur feedback use karke humne apna product bundle adjust kiya, toh na yeh learning hui ki pehle sunna padta hai, baad mein bechna padta hai, aur ek aur cheez jo seekhi woh rapport build karna, matlab chalo sales pitch chal rahi hai but thoda personal connect banana bohot zaroori hota hai, toh ab mai yeh dono cheeze consciously implement karta hoon, not just business mein but clubs aur group projects mein bhi.
Thanks. Walk me through your career so far, with a focus on your last couple of roles.

Haan, toh main apna career thoda bata deta hoon, matlab after BCom woh toh maine NM College se kiya Mumbai mein, fir directly family business join kiya tha Surat mein, jo ki Agarwal Textiles hai, yeh ek synthetic sarees ka manufacturing and trading ka business hai. Pehle ek saal toh main trainee tha, matlab literally har department mein ghooma, production dekha, accounts bhi, even factory floor pe bhi kaam kiya, toh basics samjhe pura, uske baad main business development lead ban gaya.

Wahan main jo main focus liya tha na woh naya naya sales channels dhoondne par aur exports push karne par tha, kyunki hum log pehle bilkul limited the Gujarat aur Maharashtra tak, toh phir main thoda market research kiya, exporters se milke poocha kaunsi country mein demand hai, baad mein bangladesh, Sri Lanka, aur UAE ke buyers ko target kiya, unko samples bheje, thoda personal connect kiya, us process mein maine yeh bhi seekha ki har market ka apna ek taste hota hai, matlab Bangladesh ke buyers ko darker colours pasand hai, Sri Lanka mein lightweight fabric chahiye, toh customize bhi kiya offering ko.

Dusra jaise digital process lana, woh covid ke time realize hua ki physical order dena time-consuming hai, fir maine WhatsApp catalogue banaya, sab dealers ko train kiya ki apna order WhatsApp pe bheje, toh usse kaafi jaldi processing hone laga, matlab jo pehle teen din lagte the woh same day mein ho ja raha tha. Saath mein jo negotiation skills aayi especially yarn contracts mein, Reliance ke suppliers ke saath dealing ki, bhaari volume tha toh thoda pressure bhi tha, lekin waisa bhi manage karna padta.

Phir Asian Paints ka summer internship aaya MBA ke baad, Nagpur region mein tha, wahan sales distribution ka exposure mila, basically ground pe utar ke, toh dealers aur painters ke saath kaam kiya, loyalty program launch kiya, usse engagement badhi, aur jo ek MTP top-up route ka project kiya, waisa operational driven process seekha matlab actual field data collect karke proposed solution diya, important tha ki pilot successful raha. PPO mil gaya toh kaafi boost mila confidence ko.

Toh overall na jo bhi kiya hai abhi tak, ek mix raha hai sales ka, operations ka, thoda digital transformation ka, har jagah thoda hands-on approach rakha hai aur seekhne ki koshish ki hai, toh yeh mera career journey ab tak.
You mentioned the Asian Paints stock-out project. What did you personally analyse first when identifying the 12 fast-moving SKUs?
transcript.why: Your overview covered your progression, responsibilities, and the outcomes you mentioned across your roles. We’re moving to one specific project to understand the details behind it.

transcript.text:
Achha, toh jab yeh project mila na, pehle toh mujhe data samajhna tha ki stock-outs actually ho kitne frequently rahe hain aur kaha pe, toh sabse pehle main dealer-wise aur SKU-wise sales data mangwaya, matlab pichle 3-6 mahine ka secondary sales aur inventory movement ka report, sab excel sheet mein bana liya. Uske baad main yeh dekh raha tha ki kis product ki demand zyadah hai aur kis pe regular stock-out aa raha hai, toh main ratio nikalke dekha, jaise ki out-of-stock events per SKU, aur then overall contribution to lost sales. Jahaan pe lag raha tha ki chhote chhote product hai but wahaan demand peak par hai, woh sab list banayi. 

Main khud ground par gaya aur dealers se bhi baat kiya, poocha ki bhaiyya, sabse zyada kis cheez ka demand hai aur kiska stock jaldi finish ho jata hai -- kuch toh voh bolte bhi the ki yeh 10 litre ka emulsion ya yeh putty jaldi bik jaata hai lekin stock nahi aata timely. Toh uske basis par jo 12 SKUs short-list hua woh basically mix tha paints ka, putty ka, thinners ka... aur actually us mein se bhi 4-5 SKUs repeatedly issue aa raha tha alag-alag dealers ke saath.

Toh summary mein, pehle toh excel mein sales aur inventory data analyze kiya, patterns dekhe, fir qualitative feedback liya dealers aur company sales officers se, dono ko merge karke woh 12 fast-movers identify kiya jinka stock-out business ko zyada impact kar raha tha.
Which decision was personally yours when you turned those findings into the weekly top-up route?
transcript.why: Your answer explained how you combined sales data with dealer feedback, so I asked which decision in turning that analysis into a weekly route was personally yours.

transcript.text:
Matlab, ismein jo sabse main decision meri taraf se tha na, woh yeh tha ki instead of waiting for monthly beat plan, hum log ek naya micro top-up route try karein jo specially un 12 fast-movers ke liye ho, baaki ke liye nahi. Matlab, jo normally hota kya hai ki distributor aur area sales executive ki monthly ya fortnightly routing hoti hai sab dealers pe, ek hi saath sab products ke liye order lete hain aur supply dete hain, but yeh fast-movers waale products mein dekha ki demand unpredictable hai, weekends ya local festival ke aas-paas spike aa jata hai.

Maine yeh propose kiya tha ki ek pilot karein, jahaan pe har week ek extra gaadi niklegi sirf in SKUs ke liye, order collection bhi WhatsApp pe ya call pe ho jaaye by Wednesday, Thursday tak supply ho jaaye, toh matlab business as usual disturb nahi ho par yeh critical SKUs jaldi reach ho jaye dealers tak. Plus, maine insist kiya ki yeh route logistics ke saath kaam karein, matlab truck ek extra chakkar lage, lekin mix pe focus rahe -- jo dealers repeatedly in SKUs ka stock-out face kar rahe hain, pehle unko cover karo.

Aur ek chhota sa tweak bhi maine suggest kiya tha, ki weekly top-up ke liye minimum order quantity bahut kam rakh lein, jaise 2 doodh dabba type ka, so ki dealers hesitant na ho place karne mein. Isse response achha aaya.

Toh main decisions jo mujhe lagta hai personally maine push kiya -- ek toh micro weekly route sirf fast-movers ke liye, doosra, low MOQ tak limit karna, aur teesra, pilot mein khud daily follow-ups kiya with logistics aur dealers, ki koi operational bottleneck aa toh turant solve kar saken.
Understood. Let’s move to your export work at Agarwal Textiles. How did opening the Bangladesh, Sri Lanka and UAE markets come about?
transcript.why: Your answer clarified which decisions and actions were personally yours in the top-up pilot. I moved on because the next topic covers another significant claim from your experience.

transcript.text:
Haan toh sir actually yeh export waala jo kaam hua na, woh thoda accidental bhi tha aur thoda deliberate bhi, matlab pehle toh honestly hum log sirf domestic pe hi focus karte the, mostly Gujarat aur Maharashtra ke distributors ke through. Lekin covid ke baad market kaafi stagnant ho gaya tha, domestic orders slow ho rahe the, toh tab papa and chachu dono bole ki kuch naya try karte hain, and mujhe bhi laga abhi badiya time hai explore karne ka.

Main waise ek exporter conference attend kiya tha Surat mein, wahaan pe kuch export houses ke log mil gaye, toh unse generally poocha ki synthetic sarees ka demand kahan hai Indian market ke bahar. Unhone bataya ki Bangladesh aur Sri Lanka mein kaafi demand hai because unko affordable aur colourful sarees chahiye, plus unka logon ka taste Indian style kafi pasand aata hai.

Toh fir main online, IndiaMART aur alibaba pe buyer leads search kiya, outreach chalu kiya -- pehle cold email, LinkedIn aur thoda trade body contacts, matlab idhar-idhar sab jugad kiya. Kuch buyers ne revert kiya, pehle samples bheje, phir WhatsApp pe regular coordination hota tha, unko portfolio samjhaya, rates discuss kiya, shipping ka bhi pura process inko bataya. Bangladesh ke ek buyer ne toh first sample ke baad 400 pieces ka order diya tha and woh repeat ho gaya.

Sri Lanka mein jo buyers hain wahan feedback aaya ki unko light-weight aur soft finish chahiye so humne apne loom par waisa design run kiya, catalogue bana kar bheja. Trial orders chote the, but repeat milne laga. Basically ek learning yeh hui ki apna normal stock har market ke liye fit nahi baithta, thoda customization zaroori hai.

UAE mein thoda alag tha, wahan par mainly Indian expat audience target tha, toh wahan ke ek distributor ko approach kiya jo Mumbai ke event mein mila tha, usne genuinely help kiya entry mein. Qatar aur Oman bhi try kiya tha but returns nahi mil paye.

Saath hi yeh export process mein documentation waali kaafi cheezein seekhi, jaise LC open karna, INR-USD ke conversion se risk manage karna, freight ka coordination, aur export samples ke approvals bhi face kiye.

Toh overall pehle market mapping kiya, har market mein jo fit tha woh offering adjust ki, kaafi follow ups and thoda patience laga, but jab ek baar unko trust dikh gaya delivery aur quality ka, fir order flow steady ho gaya.
You described the buyer outreach and repeat orders clearly. How was the increase from 4% to 19% of revenue calculated?

Maine yeh propose kiya tha ki ek pilot karein, jahaan pe har week ek extra gaadi niklegi sirf in SKUs ke liye, order collection bhi WhatsApp pe ya call pe ho jaaye by Wednesday, Thursday tak supply ho jaaye, toh matlab business as usual disturb nahi ho par yeh critical SKUs jaldi reach ho jaye dealers tak. Plus, maine insist kiya ki yeh route logistics ke saath kaam karein, matlab truck ek extra chakkar lage, lekin mix pe focus rahe -- jo dealers repeatedly in SKUs ka stock-out face kar rahe hain, pehle unko cover karo.

Aur ek chhota sa tweak bhi maine suggest kiya tha, ki weekly top-up ke liye minimum order quantity bahut kam rakh lein, jaise 2 doodh dabba type ka, so ki dealers hesitant na ho place karne mein. Isse response achha aaya.

Toh main decisions jo mujhe lagta hai personally maine push kiya -- ek toh micro weekly route sirf fast-movers ke liye, doosra, low MOQ tak limit karna, aur teesra, pilot mein khud daily follow-ups kiya with logistics aur dealers, ki koi operational bottleneck aa toh turant solve kar saken.
